$comment: THE CLASSIFICATION OF EVERY FIXTURE FAMILY THE MAQUETTE ENGINE DECLARES, and it is TOTAL: a family the extractor finds and this file does not name is a violation, and so is a name here the extractor cannot find. That is what makes the guard reading it impossible to pre-satisfy — it holds a NAMED INVENTORY, never a count. A floor placed at today's number is satisfied by construction on the day it is written and can only ever catch a later decrease, which is the shape B-075 found five times over. Regenerate the inventory with `node scripts/extract-maquette-fixtures.mjs --list`; the CLASS is a judgement and is never generated.

$classes.served: server state — the operator's system holds it. A seed derives from it and a handler serves it
$classes.asset: artwork, poster and trailer maps — served as part of a media payload, never as a resource of its own
$classes.interface: WHAT THE INTERFACE OWNS and a server must never send: labels, tones, orderings, icon paths, page sizes, timings. Routing one of these through a mock would have the interface asking a server for its own words. They stay where they are; L09 moves the copy to i18n and the rest into the components. The class is defined by OWNERSHIP rather than by being words — a long-press delay belongs to the interface exactly as a label does
$classes.unserved: not served, with the reason written out

$anonymous.why: pure literals declared inside an ANONYMOUS function. They are not inventoried — a name built on a line number is renamed by every edit above it — and the count is held here so their exclusion is a figure somebody compares rather than a figure somebody printed.

APPARENCES.why: the three appearance settings the interface offers

AUDIOS.why: the three audio options and their French descriptions. The option KEYS are contract values the ranking profile carries; the list and its wording are the interface's

BACK_WINDOW.why: how long the exit guard stays armed

BLOCKED.why: arrivals — what is blocked, with the reason

CADENCE_CRON.why: the grab cadence, read off the live scheduler

CATS.why: the categories and their counts, read from library.db

DECISIONS_REGLEES.why: the decisions already settled, with how each was reached

DECISION_STATE.why: the tone and the French name of each decision state

DECISION_STATE_DETAIL.why: the sentence that explains each decision state

DEPENDENCIES.why: the external dependencies and whether they answer

DISKS.why: the disks, their free space and their fill

DONE_TODAY.why: arrivals — what reached the library today

EP_LABEL.why: the French name of each episode state

EP_ORDER.why: the order episode states sort in

EP_SWATCH.why: which swatch each episode state wears

ERRORS.why: the error tally and the latest one

FOLLOWS.why: the twelve follows with their true states, read from acquire.db

GROUPS.why: how follows are grouped, and what each group is called. The status values it lists are contract vocabulary; the grouping is the interface's

INCOMPLETE.why: incomplete series with their owned/aired fractions

LIBRARY.why: the library listing — 345 of the 1 861 titles library.db holds

LIB_PAGE.why: how many tiles a library page holds

LIB_TOTAL.why: how many titles the library really holds, read from library.db

MAINT_ACTIONS.why: the maintenance action catalogue — the backend already serves one at /api/maintenance/actions

MAINT_TOPICS.why: the six maintenance rubrics, their French names and the sentence explaining each. It was classified `served` and it is the same shape as GROUPS and RISQUES, both `interface`: the backend holds the TOKEN a rubric is keyed by and never its wording. Classifying it served invented a whole demand — an operation asking a server for the interface's own rubric names.

MOVING.why: staging — what is moving through the pipeline

NOTFOUND.why: arrivals — what no release satisfies, loaded scenario

NOTFOUND_REAL.why: arrivals — what no release satisfies, real scenario

OWNED.why: owned episode numbers, season by season, for 247 series

PENDING_DECISIONS.why: the decisions still awaiting arbitration, with their candidates

PIPELINE.why: the last run, told as its nine steps, with the counts pipeline_run recorded

PRESS_MS.why: how long a press must last to be a long press

PRESS_TOLERANCE.why: how far a finger may travel and still be a press

REASON_DETAIL.why: the sentence that explains each reason

REASON_LABEL.why: the French name of each decision reason

RECENT.why: the twelve most recently added titles

RELEASES.why: the release candidates. NOT REAL — no tracker is queried (README, What is real in here) — but a release list IS server state, so it is served and the register says where its values came from

RESOLUTIONS.why: the resolution options the quality profile offers. The VALUES are contract tokens; the list is the interface's, like AUDIOS

RISQUES.why: how risky a maintenance action is, and what that is called

SCHEDULERS.why: the schedulers, their cadence and their last pass

SEASONS.why: season and episode counts per series

SECRETS.why: the secret keys and whether each is defined — never a value

SETTINGS.why: the configuration schema, section by section and field by field

SETTLED.why: staging — what has settled, loaded scenario

SETTLED_REAL.why: staging — what has settled, real scenario

SHEETS_OLD.why: a superseded media-sheet shape. Nothing reads it: the only reference outside its own declaration is the Object.assign that publishes 254 names on window for the harness, and no rule and no module names it. It dies with the engine (L13)

SHEETS_RAW.why: the media sheets — title, year, rating, synopsis, cast, provider ids, status

STARTUP_MS.why: how long the splash is held

STRIP_LABELS.why: the five pipeline positions, named in French for the strip that draws them

STUCK.why: staging — the folders the pipeline could not name, loaded scenario

STUCK_REAL.why: staging — the folders the pipeline could not name, real scenario

ST_LABEL.why: the French name of each follow status

ST_LABEL_MOVIE.why: the same three statuses said differently for a film

SUGGESTIONS.why: the suggestion deck, produced by the engine actually executing a TMDB call

SUG_BATCH.why: how many suggestions a deck batch holds

TAKEABLE.why: arrivals — what is ready to be grabbed

TODAY.why: THE PROTOTYPE'S FROZEN CLOCK, and it is the determinism device rather than data. A server does not send today's date. It is not seeded — the mock layer declares its own instant (D-L08-8) and R85 holds that the two AGREE, because every date-derived state moves the moment they do not

TRIS.why: the six sort names, each way round

URGENCY.why: the order statuses sort in — an interface decision, not a datum

VIA_LABEL.why: how a decision was reached, said in French

factRowsHTML.TONS.why: the mapping from the operator's word for a tone to the stylesheet's. Declared inside factRowsHTML, so it carries a qualified name

icons.why: the interface's own icon paths. A server never sends a drawing

openJourneySheet.steps.why: one torrent's journey, told as its five stages. Declared inside openJourneySheet, so it carries a qualified name — it is real state a contract must serve, and leaving it out would have meant copying it into a seed by hand

openPopEp.popoverWidth.why: a measurement openPopEp works with, not data

plages.out.why: an accumulator plages() fills, empty at its declaration

screenStack.why: an accumulator the engine pushes onto. `const` binds the array, never its contents, so its literal value is an empty start and not a fact
